cards.text: VEL-MERIDIAN-ORGANIZED-01 — ZEDE "STOP RUMMAGING" → THE MERIDIAN

cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: 15s vertical, mid-funnel. Mirror of the Zede Pont-des-Arts "Stop rummaging" ad, rebuilt for the Meridian Leather Tote in taupe. Same four beats, same type treatment, same black end cards. The reference's line ("this bag is organized by design") reads for any bag on the market and was replaced with the Meridian's actual interior architecture: a zip pocket running down the middle that splits the bag into two halves, demonstrated on screen in the beat where it is said. VO v2, rewritten to clear the AI-copy blacklist (v1 was a fragment stack): 'Stop rummaging.' / 'There's a zip pocket down the middle, so your laptop never ends up on top of your keys.' / 'It's called the Meridian, and Velantra has it in six colors.' HOLD FOR INVENTORY: all six colorways are oversold (~1,760 units net) and still selling.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: VO: "Stop rummaging."  TYPE: STOP RUMMAGING (word by word)
Bag closed on a dark wood tabletop, three-quarter front, plain warm wall. Locked camera, near static.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Flat interrupt. The line does the work, the picture just holds still.

Product on screen from frame one.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: VO: "This bag is organized by design."  TYPE: BAG IS / ORGANIZED BY / DESIGN (active line bright, others dimmed)
Top-down into the open bag, blue lining. A hand loads a phone into a slip pocket, reaches into a second compartment, sets a pouch down. Frame locked, only the hand moves.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Relief. This is the whole ad.

The one beat that sells. Everything else is texture.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: No VO. No type. Music only.
From behind, a woman walking away down a bright corridor, bag worn on her back. Slow follow. She reaches back to adjust a strap.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Aspiration, quiet. Proof it gets carried.

Deliberately text-free so the eye rests.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: No VO. No type.
Bag alone again on a pale wood tabletop, side on, static hero with a slow drift.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Settled. Look at the object.

Warm light, same room language as the open.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: TYPE: SHOP NOW, then the wordmark.
Full black. White centered caps, then the brand wordmark alone.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Clean stop.

Two cards, roughly 1.3s and 1.0s.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: VO: "Stop rummaging."  TYPE: STOP RUMMAGING (word by word)

Meridian in taupe, closed, three-quarter front, on a dark walnut tabletop, plain warm wall, soft window light from the left. Handles upright, side straps buckled, silver turn-lock plate centered and catching light. Locked camera, very slow push in.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Flat interrupt, same as the reference. Let the still object hold the frame.

Built image-to-image from the real taupe product photography, then a slow Ken Burns in post.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: VO (1.6 to about 6.6s): "There's a zip pocket down the middle, so your laptop never ends up on top of your keys."  TYPE: IT ZIPS / DOWN THE / MIDDLE (active line bright, others dimmed, card holds to 6.4s)

Straight down into the open Meridian, same table, same light. Sides relaxed outward so both open halves and the zip pocket between them read in one look. Three moves, about a second each: laptop slides into the left half, a hand drops a phone and keys into the right half, a hand runs the center zip closed. Frame never moves, only the hand.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Relief. Everything lands where it belongs and nothing is stacked on anything.

The zip must be unmistakable, dead centre, running the full length. Stills only, hand included in the still. Open bag plus a hand in frame is what video generation breaks. The line runs about a second past this cut on purpose.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: Tail of the line lands over the first second here, then music alone.

From behind, a woman walking away down a bright corridor with tall windows. Meridian on its detachable shoulder strap, riding at the hip, handles upright and holding their shape. Slow dolly following her, bag the sharpest thing in frame.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Aspiration, quiet. She is going somewhere and it came with her.

DEVIATION: reference bag is a backpack, the Meridian is a top-handle tote, so the strap goes on the shoulder. Framing and move unchanged. One still with a push-in, or a real phone-shot walking clip, which would be better.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: VO at 9.8s: "It's called the Meridian, and Velantra has it in six colors."  No type.
Meridian closed, side on, on a pale oak tabletop against a plain wall. Slow push in.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Settled. This is the object, this is its name.

DEVIATION: the reference has no VO here. The brand has to land somewhere for anyone watching with sound, and the colour count gives the line something to carry besides the name. Six is verified: Brown, Midnight Black, Coffee Brown, Cream, Taupe, Burgundy.

cards.title: SCRIPT
cards.text: TYPE: SHOP NOW, then VELANTRA.
Full black. White centered caps, then the wordmark alone. Mirrors the reference exactly.

cards.title: EMOTION
cards.text:
Clean stop.

Burned in post. The word Meridian and the wordmark never go near a generator.

cards.title: OURS — The Meridian Leather Tote, taupe  ·  VEL-MERIDIAN-ORGANIZED-01

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: VO v2, blacklist fix
cards.text: v1 read "It zips down the middle. Laptop on one side, everything else on the other." and closed on "The Meridian. Velantra." That is a fragment stack and a noun-phrase sign-off, which is the Triple Short Sentence Stack in section 1 of the AI-copy blacklist. Every spoken line is now a complete sentence and the cadence runs short, then long, then medium.

cards.title: HOLD FOR INVENTORY
cards.text: Every Meridian colorway is oversold and still selling: Coffee Brown -459, Brown -376, Taupe -352, Midnight Black -275, Cream -161, Burgundy -139. Roughly 1,760 units of backorder. Ship this behind a restock date, or point it at a pre-order page that states the ship date.

cards.title: Type treatment
cards.text: White, bold, all caps, centered, soft drop shadow, sitting just below the middle of the frame. Card one arrives a word at a time. Card two is a three-line stack where the line being spoken is full white and the other two are dimmed. The walking beat and the hero beat carry no type, same as the reference.

cards.title: Music
cards.text: Runs under the whole thing and carries alone from about 6.6s to 9.8s, then again from 13.0s to the end.

cards.title: No dimensions
cards.text: No measurements anywhere in the script, because the product page publishes none. Confirm the laptop size it fits and the line gets sharper and the demo gets better, because we can show that exact laptop going in.

cards.title: Birkin-inspired
cards.text: Left out on purpose. It is live vocabulary on the Weekender and the Inspired Birkin but the Meridian page has never carried it. If wanted, it goes in the hero beat as voiceover only, never in a generation prompt.

cards.title: Price
cards.text: $124.99, verified live. Held out of the primary cut. It can go on the SHOP NOW card if a price-led version is wanted.

cards.title: Alternate opens
cards.text: Same beat sheet, only the first two cards change. B: "You shouldn't have to dig around for your keys." / "The Meridian zips down the middle, so your laptop never lands on top of them."   C: "This is what the inside of a work bag should look like." / "It zips down the middle, and the sides hold their shape instead of caving in around whatever you put inside."   D: "Everything in your bag is touching everything else right now." / "This one zips down the middle, so your laptop gets a side of its own."

cards.title: Audit
cards.text: Six-month test passes: nothing is tied to a season or a moment, and the reason to believe is hardware that will still be in the bag next year. Swap test passes on the demo: the claim is not that the bag is organized, which anyone can say, it is that this bag zips into two halves, shown happening on our product in the beat where it is said. Blacklist passes: complete sentences throughout, no fragment stack, no parallel repetition, no em dashes anywhere in the deliverable.
